text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- European Parliament Greens leader Claudia Roth in verbal duel with Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller over women's rights and Islam.
- Some civil servants and pensioners given fake pay cheques. Islamist-led government has announced it would pay salaries ahead of the Eid al-Adha holiday beginning on Friday.
- Istanbul Chamber of Commerce says private schools should be tax free.
- Popular music stars Burak Kut, a Turk, and Greece's Sakis Rouvas will give a concert on the Green Line of the divided island of Cyprus.
- Turkish soldiers will arrive in Tirana to join the multinational force on April 25.
- Two rebel ministers in the secularist wing of the cabinet meet governors to urge the implementation of anti-Islamist measures.
- Companies give cement producers until May 1 to drop their prices or face boycott.
- Former head prosecutor at Ankara's state security court defends the widespread use of telephone bugging and said it is in keeping with the law.
